title: My wife draws, I design: we made a psychedelic audio-reactive runner together
author: HexshroomGame
selftext:
A few months ago, I was staring at my 2-year-old listening to Ms. Rachel sing "I'm So Happy" for the 300th time, and as my mind went numb, I thought to myself: Am I happy? Of course I am, I thought. I have a beautiful wife, a decent job, and a toddler boy who rains a roulette of chaos and joy on my every waking moment. So why, then, did I feel unfulfilled? Well, life was stagnant and predictable. Good by all measures of what is healthy, but it was routine.

I realized I needed to do something different. When I was young, I was certain making video games would be my path forward. I took AP Computer Science way back in high school and studied IT for a while in college, but life happens, housing markets crash, parents lose their jobs, and sometimes we seek out stability. Aside from being a general tech enthusiast, my foray into that world mostly ended there. I work in construction now; it pays decent enough to support a family and I enjoy the work, even if it wasn't always my original plan.

Recently, I started messing around on Google's AI Studio and eventually Claude, where I was quickly amazed by how advanced these tools had become and how much they helped me dust off my old coding foundations. Emboldened by these new tools, I realized maybe routine doesn't have to be my only path forward—maybe my passions of old can be new again.

Enter Hexshroom, a project I probably became way too obsessed with. It's a collaboration between myself and my wife, who is a talented artist and hand-drew all the original 2D artwork, which I then turned into 3D models with AI-assisted tools. The game is a combination of a few of our passions: psychedelic art, EDM, and fast-paced arcade games.

You play as a Shroom Runner collecting spores and mushrooms in a psychedelic hexagon tunnel to bring light back to your village. The 6-sided navigation is challenging for some, but really fulfilling once you nail the mechanics and can just zone into the visuals and music. Music is a big part of the game—every level is designed around its individual track. All of the main soundtrack is licensed and human-made, except for a separate Streamer Mode with AI-generated music so players can stream without getting hit with a copyright claim.

There's a 20-level campaign with increasing speed and mushroom power-up chaos, as well as an Endless Mode for chasing high scores.

Anyway, I'm really proud of the game and I've had a lot of fun making it. Flip or flop, we're not done. Right now there are 8 characters and 4 worlds, and my wife has no plans to stop drawing—so as long as there is a modicum of success, we'll continue adding to it. And if it crashes and burns, I'm sure we'll be on to the next one.

I hope some of you play it, though. The first 5 levels are free on my website (Desktop and headphones recommended):

[https://hexshroom.com](https://hexshroom.com/)

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5415590/Hexshroom/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5415590/Hexshroom/)

comments.body: I’d love to hear what other devs think, especially about the 6-sided controls. Does the movement click for you, or does it take a few tries?

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: How fun. Cool project for you two! Keep it up and keep us updated!
